opening: Kimodo-Policy adapts Kimodo's pretrained motion prior for visually grounded, closed-loop humanoid control. We describe its root--body--hand architecture and visual conditioning (Sec.~\ref{sec:method_architecture}), motion-prior transfer and history-conditioned control (Sec.~\ref{sec:t2m_transfer}), and training and inference (Sec.~\ref{sec:training_inference}). Background on Kimodo and ControlNet is provided in Appendix~\ref{sec:preliminaries}.

architecture:
\textbf{Three-Stage Architecture.}
As shown in Figure~\ref{fig:method_architecture}, Kimodo-Policy extends Kimodo's~\cite{kimodo} pretrained generator with dedicated root, body, and hand stages. LLM2Vec~\cite{behnamghader2024llm2veclargelanguagemodels} encodes instructions; frozen DINOv3~\cite{dinov3} extracts visual features. Trainable ControlNet-Root and ControlNet-Body inject these features via Dual-Path Fusion into their corresponding frozen Kimodo denoisers, which also condition on instruction embeddings and motion history. The root stage predicts global translation and heading; their local representation conditions articulated body generation. Trainable HandNet predicts bilateral hand controls from future body features, visual features, and the current bilateral hand state. All root-to-body conditioning is detached, blocking body-stage gradients to Kimodo-Root and ControlNet-Root. HandNet's body and visual inputs are also detached, so hand supervision cannot update Kimodo-Body or either ControlNet branch. These boundaries isolate stage optimization while preserving forward dependencies. Root and body predictions are converted into whole-body tracking references and executed alongside hand commands.
